speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe your double vision—does it improve when you close one eye, and is it constant or intermittent? Additionally, do you experience any drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. Have you ever experienced episodes where your vision became double or your muscles weakened suddenly, only to return to normal after a few minutes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
